Shri Akhil Godha, learned counsel for respondents No.
 ORDER

The Insurance Company / appellant has filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 01.11.2019 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ujjain (M.P.) in Claim Case No.34/2019.
2.

The only contention raised by learned counsel for the Insurance Company / appellant is that the deduction of 1/3rd is not correct and proper, in light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 as well as National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Referring to para 13 of the award, the counsel submits that while assessing the income of the deceased Shubham,
the Claims Tribunal after determining the notional income of the deceased and adding of 40% for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17417 2 MA-1231-2020 future prospects, deducted 1/3rd of the amount for the personal expenses of the deceased.
This resulted in a total compensation of Rs.13,40,472/-.

By referring para 32 of the decision in the case of Sarla Verma (Supra) , he submits that in such cases, where the deceased is a bachelor, 50% should be deducted under the head of personal expenses instead of 1/3rd.
2.1 He submits that in the subsequent case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , the Hon'ble Court has laid down the same ratio of law.
Thus, he further submits that the ultimate quantum of compensation is higher due to the mistake committed by the Claims Tribunal.
He refers to the order passed by the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Smt. Gurkho Bai and Others vs. Kuver Singh and Others passed in M.A. No.759/2016 on 22.01.2019.

sentences.text: Therefore, he submits that the compensation should be reduced by deducting 50% from the income of the deceased for his personal expenses.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 / claimants submit that the entire family was dependent solely on the income of the deceased.

He further submits referring to para 7 of the cross-examination of Shivkanya (PW-1), the mother of the deceased, that the father of the deceased is indisposed due to ill health and thus, does not contribute to the family's support.

Consequently,
the entire family was entirely dependent on the income of the deceased.
He submits that considering the peculiar facts of this case, the deduction of 1/3rd was just and proper.

He also submits that the Claims Tribunal, while quantifying the compensation under various heads, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17417 3 MA-1231-2020 did not award any amount under the head of consortium.
Furthermore, he submits that the amounts awarded for loss of estate and funeral expenses were also inadequate.

4. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
5.
From a bare reading of the assessment done by the Claims Tribunal in para 13 of the award, it can be seen that under the head of personal expenses, 1/3rd has been deducted.
It is also undisputable in view of the evidence available on record that the deceased was a bachelor.

However, this case has some peculiar circumstances : (i) the deceased was only a labourer;
(ii) nothing has been awarded for loss of consortium and meager amount has been awarded in otherheads and (iii) apart from him, only father and mother are there, both are not in good health.
The father is undergoing continuous treatment and is unemployed, resulting in severe financial hardship for the family, they are living in penury.
In light of these peculiar circumstances, this Court does not find it appropriate to interfere with the quantum of compensation.
While it is true that for a bachelor, ordinarily 50% should be deducted, the Court refrains from altering the quantum decided by the Claims Tribunal, owing to the specific facts of this case.
Consequently, the present appeal is dismissed.

6. Considering the peculiar circumstances of this case, the Insurance Company will pay interest only up to the date of stay i.e. 21.02.2022 when the execution was stayed by this Court with a stipulation that the Insurance Company will deposit 60% of the amount.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17417 4 MA-1231-2020 7.
With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands dismissed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt Shivkanyabai on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95748886/
